title: The science of baking: weigh, balance and control your oven

say: The science of baking: weigh, balance, and control your oven.
This is the video for module one of Advanced Baking and Pastry.
Professional bakers do not follow recipes blindly. They work in weights and ratios, and decide how much gluten they want.

panel.heading: Professionals understand, not just follow
items: Work in grams and baker's percentages

say: They know what each ingredient does, and they make an ordinary oven bake the same way every time.

panel.heading: Professionals understand, not just follow
items: Work in grams and baker's percentages

say: One cup of flour can weigh anywhere from about 120 to 150 grams, depending on how it is scooped. So weigh everything, on a scale that reads in 1 gram steps.

panel.heading: Flour is always 100%
items: Divide each weight by the flour weight
To scale: new flour x percentage / 100

say: For example, Ngozi in Enugu makes dinner rolls with 500 grams of flour and 300 grams of water. 300 divided by 500 is 0.60.

say: Times 100 gives 60 percent water. Her full formula is 100 percent flour, 60 water, 2 salt, 1 yeast, 8 sugar and 6 butter.

say: A caterer orders three times as much. 1,500 grams of flour times 60, divided by 100, is 900 grams of water. The whole dough is 2,655 grams, which makes 44 rolls of 60 grams.

say: Now if a recipe online shows 6 percent salt, you will spot the error before you waste a bag of flour.

panel.rule: Normal bread: salt about 2%, instant yeast about 1%

say: Flour plus water, mixed, makes gluten, a stretchy network. Bread needs lots. Cakes and pastry need little, or they turn tough. Choose flour by protein: about 12 to 14 percent for bread, 7 to 9 for soft cakes.
Less water, as in shortcrust, means less gluten.
Kneading builds gluten, so for cakes, mix flour only until it disappears.
Fat coats the proteins and blocks them from joining.
And sugar holds on to water, while acids like buttermilk tenderise.
Flour and eggs build structure. Too few eggs, and the cake sinks or crumbles. Too many, and it turns rubbery.
Fat and sugar tenderise. Change one side and you must think about the other.
For example, Halima in Kaduna cut sugar by 20 percent. She added 25 grams more milk for moisture, and checked the cake earlier, because less sugar means less browning.
All lift comes from air, steam or carbon dioxide. Baking powder carries its own acid. The guide is about 1 level teaspoon per 125 grams of flour.

panel.heading: Check the leavener against a guide
items: Baking powder: about 1 tsp per 125 g flour
Baking soda: about a quarter tsp
Soda needs an acid in the recipe
Too much: rises, sinks, tastes bitter

say: Baking soda is much stronger. About a quarter teaspoon per 125 grams.

say: For example, Bisi in Ibadan found a red velvet recipe for 750 grams of flour with 3 teaspoons of soda. The guide is 1.5. Her cakes sank and tasted bitter.
She reduced it to 1.5 teaspoons of soda and 3 of baking powder. The next cakes had level tops and no bitter taste. And keep leaveners labelled, on a high shelf, away from children.

say: Many ovens have no accurate thermostat. Do not trust the dial. Place an oven thermometer in the centre of the middle shelf.

panel.heading: Calibrate, map, then write a card
items: Oven thermometer on the middle shelf
Heat 20 minutes, read the real temperature

say: Set the oven and wait at least 20 minutes, then read the real temperature.

say: Repeat at three settings. For example, Grace in Port Harcourt found mark 4 on her gas cooker reads 175 degrees.

say: Spread slices of white bread on a tray. The ones that toast first show hot spots. Grace's base ran hot, so she now puts an empty tray below her cakes as a shield.

say: She wrote it all on a card near the oven, and stopped burning cake bases. Test doneness properly too: a clean skewer and a top that springs back.

say: Before you bake, know the safety rules. Light a gas oven exactly as the maker instructs, with the door open.

cards.d: Light a gas oven exactly as the maker instructs, with the door open.
Turn off gas at the cylinder. Light nothing, no switches. Open windows and get it checked.
Keep a fire blanket or suitable extinguisher. Use thick, dry oven gloves, never a damp cloth.

say: If you smell gas, turn it off at the cylinder. Do not light anything or switch on lights. Open windows and doors, and get the leak checked before using the oven again.

cards.d: Light a gas oven exactly as the maker instructs, with the door open.
Turn off gas at the cylinder. Light nothing, no switches. Open windows and get it checked.
Keep a fire blanket or suitable extinguisher. Use thick, dry oven gloves, never a damp cloth.

say: Keep a fire blanket or a suitable fire extinguisher in the kitchen. And use thick, dry oven gloves. A damp cloth transfers heat and can burn you.

say: To remember. Weigh in grams and use baker's percentages. Control gluten with water, mixing, fat and sugar. Balance builders and tenderisers.
Check leaveners against the guide. And trust an oven thermometer, not the dial.

items: Water, mixing, fat and sugar control gluten

Trust a thermometer, not the dial
